points.description: Rural communities/slow growth or primarily forested
Single family homes/suburban
Rapidly urbanizing/urban
No development or no potential for impacts.
Moderate development or moderate potential for impacts, but none within 1 mile of project reach.
High development or potential for impacts in contributing watershed or within 1 mile of project reach, or high potential of impacts >1 mile away from project reach.
Floodplain is actively engaged at the local moderate-flood standard (often about 1-2 yr or 2-5 yr).
Overbanking requires flows slightly larger than typical bankfull, but still not rare. / Overbanking requires 5-10 yr floods. Partial disconnection.
Rarely or never overbanking below about 10+ yr events. Deep incision or levees block moderate floods.
Beaver dams or small ponds enhance baseflow and habitat with negligible fragmentation.
1-2 small obstructions with minor impacts. / Multiple ponds moderately disrupt connectivity.
Widespread channel fragmentation or overabundant ponding.
Multiple off-channel features connect in moderate floods.
Partial connection or fewer off-channel areas. / Only large floods access these areas, or off-channel areas are minimal.
Off-channel features are mostly gone or permanently cut off.
>5% wetland coverage, or consistent with historical norm.
1-5% wetland coverage.
<1% wetland coverage, or heavily drained wetlands.
0-1 outfall per 100 m, and no noticeable discharge effects.
2-3 outfalls per 100 m, with some unmitigated runoff but partial buffering. / 4-5 outfalls per 100 m, with noticeable sediment or pollutant inputs.
More than 5 outfalls per 100 m, or major highway drains with concentrated discharge.
No significant withdrawals or returns. Flows remain near natural.
Minor ditches or returns with limited effect. / Moderate diversions or returns causing seasonal stress.
Large or chronic diversions or returns that drastically alter the flow regime.
No CDPS permitted facilities upstream of the project reach.
CDPS permitted facilities comprise a low to moderate percentage of the baseflow in the project reach AND no facilities are located within 2 miles upstream of project reach.

CDPS permitted facilities comprise a high percentage of the baseflow in the project reach OR 1 or more facilities present within 2 miles upstream of project reach have a high potential to threaten aquatic life.
Tributaries are mostly natural with stable flows and sediment loads consistent with reference conditions.
1-2 tributaries are moderately altered or somewhat polluted. / Multiple tributaries are significantly altered and deliver high sediment or pollutants.
Widespread severe tributary impacts that overwhelm the mainstem.
RBI ? 25% quartile value and ?75% quartile value.
RBI declining over time and approaching 25% quartile value, or increasing and approaching the 75% quartile value.
RBI <25% quartile value or >75% quartile value.
<10% difference from baseline.
10-50% difference.
>50% difference. Near dewatering or strong hydropeaking.
Flow permanence is stable and near the historical pattern for the stream type.
Minor changes in dry or wet intervals. / Significant changes in flow permanence (for example a formerly perennial reach goes dry for extended periods).
Major departure from reference flow permanence. Flow regime category is effectively changed.
Aufeis formation caused by land disturbance is minor or nonexistent within, extends into the reach from downstream, or is found upstream of the project reach.
Aufeis formation caused by land disturbance is moderate within, extends into the reach from downstream, or is found within 1 kilometer (0.62 miles) upstream of the project reach.
Aufeis formation caused by land disturbance is extensive within, extends into the reach from downstream, or is found within 1 kilometer (0.62 miles) upstream of the project reach.
BFI closely matches the region's baseline.
About 10-20% difference from baseline. / About 20-40% difference from baseline.
More than 40% difference from baseline, indicating extreme baseflow alteration.
>75% of channel wetted at normal low flow (or dryness is normal if ephemeral).
25-75% wetted.
<25% wetted, or mostly disconnected pools in a historically perennial reach.
About 1-2 yr floods engage the floodplain.
About 3-5 yr floods are needed. / About 5-10 yr floods are needed.
Floodplain is rarely inundated except during extreme events.
Bed mobilizes at appropriate flows for the channel type, often near bankfull.
Slight mismatch. Bed moves below or above expected flows. / Marked mismatch. Bed is often locked or frequently scoured.
Extreme mismatch. Bed rarely moves or is reworked by small floods.
Stable channel that is not incised or dredged with frequent floodplain access.
Slight channelization or partial dredging. / Heavily modified or incised channel with limited floodplain access.
Deeply dredged or channelized reach with little functional floodplain.
Multiple active features connected during moderate floods and consistent with historical complexity.
Partial complexity remains with some features truncated or partially isolated. / Most off-channel features are lost or only minimally connected.
Floodplain is simplified or leveed with little or no off-channel function remaining.
Permeable floodplain soils that support subsurface flow.
Partially permeable soils or some clogging. / Mostly fine fill or bedrock that limits infiltration.
Heavily compacted or lined soils with minimal subsurface exchange.
Well developed bedforms and strong potential for exchange.
Some bedform variety but partially uniform. / Mostly uniform run with limited exchange.
Featureless or silted bed with negligible exchange.
Stable or re-stabilized channel (Stage I or VI).
Partially recovered channel (often Stage V). / Actively widening or incising (often Stage III-IV).
Severe incision or destructive phases (often Stage II or severe III-IV).
Altered watercourse score - 71% or greater.
Altered watercourse score between 41 and 70%.
Altered Watercourse Index Score of 40% or less.
Predominantly natural banks with deeply rooted cover.
Some armoring or partial vegetation coverage. / Large portion of banks is armored or vegetation is sparse.
Failing armoring or widespread bare banks with severe instability.
Condition aligns with local reference for the stream type.
Slight departure from reference condition. / Moderate braiding where not typical, or loss of braiding where it is typical.
Heavily braided from instability, or forced single-thread where braiding is expected.
>80% of contributing streams (including tributaries) within catchment has > 25 feet corridor width.
50-80% of streams (including tributaries) within catchment has > 25 feet corridor width.
<50% of streams (including tributaries) within catchment has > 25 feet corridor width.
No active downcutting. Bed elevation is stable.
Minor localized incision. / Noticeable incision or one or two moderate headcuts that reduce floodplain access.
Severe channel-wide incision with multiple major headcuts.
No areas of permafrost degradation in the catchment area have been observed.
Areas of permafrost degradation exist within or upstream of the project reach contributing to hillslope slumping or increased erosion but are not resulting in impacts to water quality.
Areas of permafrost degradation exist within or upstream of the project reach, contributing to hillslope slumping, increased erosion, and/or water quality impacts.
Low chronic turbidity and minimal fines, or regionally normal conditions.
Minor silt layers or partial turbidity. / High turbidity or moderate silt coverage.
Severe siltation or turbidity that smothers substrate.
Low anthropogenic-caused sediment supply. Upstream bank erosion and surface runoff is minimal.
Moderate anthropogenic-caused sediment supply from upstream bank erosion and surface runoff.
High anthropogenic-caused sediment supply from upstream bank erosion and surface runoff.
Clear riffle-pool or step-pool sequence with robust variety.
Some diversity but partially uniform. / Mostly homogeneous bed with faint or missing sequences.
Flattened or artificially uniform bed.
Never had them, or no remaining evidence.
May have occurred but effects ameliorated.
Occurred and effects persist.
Open interstitial coarse bed with minimal fines.
Mild embedding or partial fine coverage. / Strong embedding or siltation limiting infiltration.
Predominantly fine or consolidated bed with little interstitial space.
Minimal algae and no nuisance mats.
Slightly elevated algal coverage. / Large mats that partially impair habitat.
Dense bloom or scum that covers substrate.
Rarely surpasses local standard or typical seasonal maxima for the stream type.
Slightly exceeds thresholds occasionally.
Frequently near or above thresholds. / Consistently high or potentially lethal temperatures.
Multiple cooler pockets or deeper pools provide refugia during warm periods.
One or two minor refuges. / Rare or minimal cooler zones.
No refugia where expected. High thermal stress risk.
Abundant CPOM retention with stable leaf packs typical for the system.
Some retention but partially flushed out. / Sparse organic matter and limited retention.
Essentially no retained organic matter, or severe overload causing anoxia risk.
Balanced growth with no nuisance blooms.
Slightly elevated algae. / Frequent moderate nuisance mats.
Thick blooms or scums that cover substrate.
There is little to no agricultural land uses or the livestock or cropland is far enough away from project reach to cause no impact to water quality or biology.
Livestock access to stream and/or intensive cropland upstream of project reach. A sufficient reach of stream is between Ag. land use and project reach.
Livestock access to stream and/or intensive cropland immediately upstream of project reach.
Strong potential with connected wet areas and soils.
Some wet zones but partially disconnected. / Limited wetland area and moderate export risk.
No wetlands or heavily drained soils with low denitrification potential.
<2 mg/L diurnal swing and no frequent hypoxia.
2-4 mg/L swing with occasional stress. / 4-6 mg/L swing and borderline low DO at night.
>6 mg/L swing or frequent dips below 3 mg/L.
Near background or guideline values.
Slightly elevated N or P. / Marked elevation with likely ecological effects.
Significantly above guidelines indicating strong nutrient pollution.
No nuisance algae and <10% cover, or normal for region.
10-30% cover or mild filaments. / 30-50% cover with partial blooms.
>50% cover or thick scums.
Natural soils with no contamination indicators.
Minor dumping or moderate manure presence. / Known moderate contamination risk.
Highly contaminated soils with strong odor or toxicity indicators.
>6 mg/L and no hypoxia.
5-6 mg/L. Borderline. / 3-5 mg/L. Frequent stress.
<3 mg/L. High risk of acute impacts.
In category 1, 2, or 3 or aquatic life uses not evaluated.
In Category 4 due to nonsupport of aquatic life uses and aquatic life impairment actively being mitigated.
In Category 5 due to nonsupport of aquatic life uses OR in Category 4 and aquatic life impairment not actively being mitigated.
Piedmont = <78; Blue Ridge = <41
Piedmont = 78-229; Blue Ridge = 41-66
Piedmont = >229; Blue Ridge = >66
Mostly clear and consistent with reference. No obvious pollution.
Slight turbidity or discoloration. / Persistent cloudiness with habitat impacts.
Persistently muddy water or visible sheen indicating severe pollution.
Multiple habitat types well represented.
Some variety but key elements are missing. / Mostly uniform with only 1-2 distinct features.
Very uniform channel with limited structural diversity.
Well connected off-channel areas provide refuge or spawning habitat.
Some partial connection. / Rare or only episodic off-channel use.
No side or backwaters remain despite suitable valley setting.
Multiple observations where historically expected.
Some presence but limited. / Rare or single individuals.
Absent where historically expected.
Greater than 60% of the total catchment area is draining to the project reach.
40 to 60% of the total catchment area is draining to the project reach.
Less than 40% of the total catchment area is draining to the project reach.
More than 40% of reach has adequate juvenile cover.
5-40% cover.
<5% cover or none.
Clean or appropriate substrate with minimal silt.
Some silt but still feasible for spawning. / Heavily silted with limited spawning success expected.
No suitable substrate. High embeddedness, bedrock, or other limiting condition.
<5% invasive presence.
5-50% invasive presence.
>50% invasive presence or one invasive dominates.
Four to five or more distinct major groups.
Two to four distinct major groups. / One to two distinct major groups.
Zero, or only one extremely tolerant group.
Channel immediately upstream or downstream of project reach (i.e., within 1 km or 0.62 mi) has native bed and bank material.
Channel immediately upstream or downstream of project reach (i.e., within 1 km or 0.62 mi) has native bed and bank material that is highly embedded by fine sediment.
Channel immediately upstream or downstream of project reach (i.e., within 1 km or 0.62 mi) is concrete, piped, or hardened.
No artificial dryness and natural connectivity is maintained.
Minor dryness in small segments. / Notable dryness or disconnection in key reaches.
Chronic or large-scale dewatering causing major fragmentation.
No barrier within watershed OR barriers provide beneficial effect on project area and allows for aquatic organism passage.
Barrier exists but does not adversely affect aquatic organism passage OR a small blockage exists that is creating a minor fish passage barrier.
Aquatic organism barriers (including impoundment(s)) located within 1 mile upstream or downstream of project area has a negative effect on aquatic organism passage.
No major levees or walls and free lateral movement.
Some partial barriers with remaining access. / Large levees hamper movement in many areas.
Heavily walled or leveed corridor with minimal lateral connectivity.
